description:
FILED s449q (Opus round-7 agent Q).  The RESIDUE of #621: the return value and
the "does it die" question are now perl's for every probed shape; only the
errno VALUE of one sub-shape differs.

REPRODUCER:

    open(BW, '<', "/etc/hostname") or die; close BW;
    my $r = open(my $x, "<&BW");
    printf "ret=%s errno=%d (%s)\n", (defined $r ? $r : "undef"), $!+0, "$!";

        perl  ret=undef errno=9  (Bad file descriptor)
        PCL   ret=undef errno=22 (Invalid argument)

perl's discriminator is whether the GLOB has an IO slot: a name that was opened
and closed keeps one (fileno -1 -> the dup fails EBADF), a name never opened has
none (EINVAL).  PCL cannot tell them apart: `%p-forget-fh` REMHASHES the name
out of `*p-filehandles*`, so a closed bareword and an unknown word look
identical, and #621's two-argument arm answers EINVAL for both.  The
never-opened case -- the one #621 was filed for -- is right; this one is not.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, both measured before choosing:
 (a) let `%p-forget-fh` leave a NIL entry for the by-NAME shapes instead of
     remhashing, so `(nth-value 1 (gethash sym *p-filehandles*))` IS perl's
     "the glob has an IO".  Free, but it changes what the two NAME-SCAN loops
     in `%p-resolve-fh` see (`return v` on a NIL value ends the scan) and what
     the glob-alias copy at cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:14874 does with `present` --
     probe both before touching it.
 (b) a dedicated `*p-closed-fh-names*` set maintained by the
     `%p-install-fh` / `%p-forget-fh` mirror pair.  Needs their three by-name
     key computations factored into one helper first (they are already three
     copies each -- rule 11).

NOT WORTH IT ON ITS OWN (project ruling: exact error text/errno is not a goal
unless cheap).  Do it if (a) turns out to be free, or fold it into whichever
task next touches the install/forget pair.  Guard row would go beside the #621
row in Pl/t/print-fh-magic-01.t.

SECOND, SMALLER RESIDUE in the same family: the THREE-argument form with an
EMPTY string source, `open(my $x, "<&", "")`, dies "Can't use an undefined
value as filehandle reference" where perl dies `Bad filehandle: ` (empty name).
Both die, only the text differs -- `%p-dup-src-name` folds the empty string in
with undef.
subject: A 2-arg dup from a CLOSED bareword handle reports EINVAL where perl reports EBADF, because PCL forgets a closed name entirely
